name: Morpheus8 Body
lead: Morpheus8 Body is the body-treatment version of InMode's Morpheus8 fractional radiofrequency (RF) microneedling system, used on areas such as the abdomen, arms and thighs for skin laxity and texture [1][2].

A 2024 plastic-surgery review lists Morpheus8 and Morpheus8 Body among RF-based minimally invasive tools used alongside surgical body contouring [3]. A registered 48-person study examined RF microneedling for leg cellulite [4].

paras: An AI-generated encyclopedia entry reports that body applications of Morpheus8 expanded around 2020 and that a 40-pin Body 3D tip is used for larger areas [1]. That account is untrusted and not independently verified here.

A 2024 article in Clinics in Plastic Surgery describes an author's use of RF devices, including Morpheus8 and Morpheus8 Body, in body-contouring practice; it is a practice description rather than a controlled trial [3]. A 48-person registered study evaluated multi-depth RF microneedling for cellulite of the leg [4]. The Grokipedia source states that independent long-term data are limited [1].
Reported effects of Morpheus8 treatments include temporary redness, swelling and pinpoint bleeding, with burns, scarring and infection listed as rarer risks [1].

card.summary: InMode's RF microneedling for larger body areas; evidence is limited to practice reports and one small registered study.

quick.overview:
Morpheus8 Body applies InMode's RF microneedling to the abdomen, arms, thighs and other areas, marketed for skin tightening and texture.

Supporting research is limited to surgeon practice descriptions and a small registered cellulite study.
quick.mechanism: Insulated needles deliver RF energy to the dermis and deeper tissue, which providers say prompts collagen remodeling.
quick.risks: Temporary redness and swelling are common; burns, scarring and infection are described as rarer risks.
